statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-13505 (GHSA-98j2-6v39-78w8): in Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (bc-fips) before 2.1.3 in the 2.1 series, the AES and DESede engines, the SP 800-90A DRBGs, SymmetricSecretKey and the PBKD and scrypt parameter classes zeroise their key material through Object.finalize. Under load the single finalizer thread can fall behind, so key material stays in the heap while queued and the queue can contribute to an OutOfMemoryError. Bouncy Castle fixed it in bc-fips 2.1.3 (also 2.0.2 and 1.0.2.7), where disposal runs from a java.lang.ref.Cleaner in the jar's Java 9 multi-release classes: https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/wiki/CVE%E2%80%902026%E2%80%9013505 and https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-98j2-6v39-78w8. Bouncy Castle lists Java 9 and later as the affected platform and says that in practice this did not bite on Java 8 or Java 11 and becomes a problem on later JVMs; this owner is a Java 11 JDK, so the practical impact is low, but the builds that ship bc-fips 2.1.2 still carry the finalizer-based code and are listed as affected. Checked every published eclipse-temurin-11-jdk-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine security repository, which is the package of this source that ships Bouncy Castle: for x86_64 (16 builds, 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.33.10-r1) and aarch64 (8 builds, 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.31.11-r6), where both architectures carry the same Bouncy Castle versions; each download matched the index checksum. Each ships five jars in /usr/lib/bouncycastle: bc-fips, bcpkix-fips, bcutil-fips, bctls-fips and bc-rng-jent. The AES, DRBG, SymmetricSecretKey and scrypt classes the advisory concerns (FipsAES, FipsDRBG and Scrypt in org.bouncycastle.crypto.fips, and org.bouncycastle.crypto.SymmetricSecretKey) are in the bc-fips jar; none of the other four jars contains a class of those names. The bc-fips version, read from each jar's manifest: 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.32.1.1-r0 carry bc-fips 2.1.2; 11.0.32.1.1-r1 carries bc-fips 2.1.3; 11.0.32.9-r0 carries bc-fips 2.1.2; 11.0.32.9.1.1-r2 to 11.0.33.10-r1 carry bc-fips 2.1.3. In every 2.1.3 jar, seven Java 9 multi-release classes under META-INF/versions/9 (among them SymmetricSecretKey and the AES, DESede and DRBG working buffers) reference java.lang.ref.Cleaner; no class in the 2.1.2 jars does. Every published eclipse-temurin-11-jdk, eclipse-temurin-11-jdk-oci-config and eclipse-temurin-11-jdk-fips-oci-config package for Alpine 3.23 contains no Bouncy Castle jar or class file. Under apk ordering 11.0.32.9-r0 sorts above the fixed 11.0.32.1.1-r1 but ships bc-fips 2.1.2, so the range needs a second affected span: up to 11.0.32.1.1-r1, and from 11.0.32.9-r0 up to 11.0.32.9.1.1-r2.

CVE-2026-13505 (GHSA-98j2-6v39-78w8): Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (bc-fips) before 2.1.3 zeroises key material held by the AES and DESede engines, the DRBGs, SymmetricSecretKey and the PBKD and scrypt parameter classes from Object.finalize, so disposal can fall behind under load and the key material stays in the heap meanwhile. 2.1.3 moves disposal to java.lang.ref.Cleaner (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-98j2-6v39-78w8, https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/wiki/CVE%E2%80%902026%E2%80%9013505). Upstream lists the affected platform as Java 9 and later and notes that in practice it did not bite on Java 11; this owner is a Java 11 runtime, but the finalizer-based code is present in the 2.1.2 builds and 2.1.3 is the upstream fix, so this is recorded as FIXED at the first build with 2.1.3 rather than as not affected. Covered every package of this owner published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repositories: eclipse-temurin-11-jre-fips on x86_64 (16 versions, 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.33.10-r1) and aarch64 (8 versions, 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.31.11-r6, the same Bouncy Castle files as the x86_64 packages of those versions), eclipse-temurin-11-jre on x86_64 (the same 16 versions; none is published for aarch64), and the oci-config packages. Read the bundle version from the manifest of every Bouncy Castle jar in every published package of this owner, recursing into nested archives. Bouncy Castle is in the eclipse-temurin-11-jre-fips package, as /usr/lib/bouncycastle/bc-fips-<version>.jar next to the bcpkix-fips, bctls-fips, bcutil-fips and bc-rng-jent jars. The eclipse-temurin-11-jre packages hold no Bouncy Castle classes, in jrt-fs.jar or in the runtime image lib/modules, and the eclipse-temurin-11-jre-oci-config packages hold no jars. bc-fips is 2.1.2 in 11.0.30.7-r0 to 11.0.32.1.1-r0 and in 11.0.32.9-r0, and 2.1.3 in 11.0.32.1.1-r1 and in 11.0.32.9.1.1-r2 and every later build. Under apk version ordering 11.0.32.9-r0 sorts between those two fixed builds, so the range has two spans: affected below 11.0.32.1.1-r1, fixed from 11.0.32.1.1-r1, affected again from 11.0.32.9-r0, and fixed from 11.0.32.9.1.1-r2.

These are eclipse-temurin-8-jdk and eclipse-temurin-8-jdk-oci-config in the DHI Alpine repository, and eclipse-temurin-8-jdk-fips and eclipse-temurin-8-jdk-fips-oci-config in the authenticated DHI Alpine security repository: 16 versions, 8.482.08-r0 to 8.512.09-r1 for x86_64; for aarch64 only the oci-config and -fips packages are published, 8.482.08-r0 to 8.492.09-r6, all with bc-fips 2.1.2. On Alpine (musl) with a Java 21 runtime, an application that registers the bc-rng-jent 1.3.6 provider itself and asks for its BCRNG ENTROPY generator gets "JENT RNG failed".
